prompt.brief: Design a metrics and log aggregation platform that collects counters, gauges, histograms, traces, and structured logs from thousands of servers, supports alerting, and controls cardinality and retention cost.
successSignals: Define metric identity, timestamp, labels, units, and aggregation semantics separately from raw log and trace envelopes.
Batch and compress at agents, enforce tenant and label budgets, shard ingestion by series, and downsample older data.
Keep alert evaluation predictable and isolate it from exploratory queries and high-cardinality ingestion.
Explain clock skew, duplicate samples, agent buffering, missing data, retention tiers, privacy, and alert correctness.

functional: Register sources and schemas, collect metric and log batches, query time ranges, aggregate series, and configure alerts.
Support counters, gauges, histograms, exemplars, structured logs, retention policies, and downsampled rollups.
Expose ingestion health, query results, alert state, missing-data indicators, cardinality warnings, and tenant usage.
nonFunctional: Target p95 ingestion acknowledgement below 1 second and query common dashboard ranges below 2 seconds.
Handle billions of data points per day with agent batching, partitioned WALs, compression, and cardinality limits.
Make samples and log batches deduplicable, preserve alert evaluation checkpoints, and distinguish missing from zero.
Buffer at agents and serve recent local or downsampled data when remote storage or query workers are degraded.
scaleAssumptions: Collect 5 million samples per second, 2 billion points per day, and logs from 10,000 hosts.
Partition by tenant, metric series, and time; isolate high-cardinality labels and noisy sources.
Retain a short-resolution hot window and compressed rollups while archiving raw logs by policy.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Metrics commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Metrics writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Metrics version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Metrics by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Metrics work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Metrics projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Metrics projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Metrics records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Metrics latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
